messages:
Evan (Onboarding): Quick heads-up  I scheduled the recurring orientation for Tue 10/19 16:00 UTC (RRULE: weekly x4) but two new hires reported odd behavior: Outlook shows an extra instance the following week and the recording link isn't in their calendar preview. Anyone run into recurring invites + timezone + recording perms weirdness? cc @zoom-bot

zoom-bot: Recurring event created by Evan. ICS attached. Note: recordings are saved to /Onboarding/Recordings and linked in the event description if organizer includes the URL.

Zara Kim: Outlook desktop is notorious for expanding RRULE differently depending on DTSTART timezone and VTIMEZONE presence. If your ICS lacks the VTIMEZONE block or uses a Z (UTC) suffix for DTSTART, Outlook sometimes creates duplicates or shifts when DST boundaries cross the series.

Noah Blake: Also seen this: if you create an RRULE in Google Calendar in the organizer's local tz (e.g., America/Los_Angeles), Google will send an ICS with DTSTART in that TZ, but some clients interpret the recurrence in UTC and you get off-by-one-day at certain locales.

IT-Sys: Short checklist: 1) include full VTIMEZONE/TZID in ICS, 2) set DTSTART with TZID (not Z), 3) include EXDATEs if you manually adjust one occurrence, 4) paste recording URL + passcode as plain text in description.

Zara Kim: If you're nervous about RRULE, another tactic is to create individual weekly events (copy event) for the number of sessions. Tedious but avoids client RRULE parsing differences.

Noah Blake: For DST-safe RRULE examples, make DTSTART like `DTSTART;TZID=America/Los_Angeles:20261019T090000` and include a matching VTIMEZONE block in the ICS. Avoid `DTSTART:20261019T160000Z` for recurring local-time events.

IT-Sys: Example ICS snippet that helped us (pasted here):

```
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
VERSION:2.0
PRODID:-//Redwood//Onboarding//EN
BEGIN:VTIMEZONE
TZID:America/Los_Angeles
X-LIC-LOCATION:America/Los_Angeles
BEGIN:STANDARD
DTSTART:19701101T020000
TZOFFSETFROM:-0700
TZOFFSETTO:-0800
TZNAME:PST
END:STANDARD
BEGIN:DAYLIGHT
DTSTART:19700308T020000
TZOFFSETFROM:-0800
TZOFFSETTO:-0700
TZNAME:PDT
END:DAYLIGHT
END:VTIMEZONE
BEGIN:VEVENT
DTSTART;TZID=America/Los_Angeles:20261019T090000
RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=4
SUMMARY:Redwood New Hire Orientation
DESCRIPTION:Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/xxxx
Passcode: 112233
Recording: will be uploaded to /Onboarding/Recordings and linked here
END:VEVENT
END:VCALENDAR
```

Noah Blake: Thanks IT-Sys : that exact VTIMEZONE approach fixed our Outlook duplicates last quarter.

Evan (Onboarding): Plan: recreate the series with explicit TZ (America/Los_Angeles for organizer), export verified ICS (confirm VTIMEZONE present), paste the Zoom URL + passcode in plain text, and publish "Add to calendar" links on the Notion onboarding page so folks can pick their client. I'll also set the recording to auto-upload and ensure ACLs allow `new-hires@redwood` group read access.

Zara Kim: One more: include a tiny per-region note in the description: "If the series falls overnight for you, DM Evan and we'll send a single-occurrence ICS or recording link." Saved us from someone attending at 2am. :grimacing:

IT-Sys: I'll pre-provision Box/Notion read for the new-hires group and confirm SSO access. If anyone still sees duplicates after Evan posts the new ICS, reply here with OS + calendar client (e.g., macOS Calendar 14 / Outlook 16 / Gmail mobile) and we'll generate a hand-exported ICS for that zone.

zoom-bot: Tip: use `gcalcli` or `icalendar` python to generate an ICS with VTIMEZONE. Example gcalcli command: `gcalcli add --when "2026-10-19 16:00" --duration 75 --title "Redwood New Hire Orientation" --description "Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/xxxx Passcode: 112233" --timezone "America/Los_Angeles" --calendar "Onboarding"` then export ICS and verify VTIMEZONE block.

Evan (Onboarding): I'll update the series and publish the Notion page with per-client add links by EOD. If anyone spots anything funky in exports (esp. Apple/Exchange), drop OS + client here and I'll hand-export. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Noah Blake: :thumbsup:

Zara Kim: :sparkles:
